indication: Persistent/recurrent AML, ALL, MDS or JMML after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: HLA-A*02:01-positive recipients with recipient HA-1(H)-positive / donor HA-1-negative mismatch; disease recurrence after allo-HCT; donor-derived product after lymphodepletion.
design: Single-arm phase 1, donor-derived HA-1 TCR-T post-HCT
intervention_dose: One or more infusions of HA-1 TCR-T (CD8+ and CD4+ cells expressing the HA-1 TCR plus a CD8 coreceptor) after lymphodepleting chemotherapy

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: achieved or maintained CR after lymphodepletion + HA-1 TCR-T; 1 patient in remission >2 years

safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicities across 9 treated recipients; TCR-T expanded and persisted in vivo. The characteristic risks in this setting are lymphodepletion cytopenias and GVHD; the full per-term AE table in the Blood 2024 full text could not be retrieved through available channels.
notes: Closest published precedent for the patient's primary handle and the same mechanism as TSC-100 (NCT05473910). Feasibility/safety phase 1, not powered for efficacy. Per-term safety table not retrievable: publisher/PMC WebFetch blocked, PMC OA efetch returned front-matter only, and NCT03326921 has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov.

intervention_label: WT1-TCRc4 EBV-specific donor CD8+ T cells (TTCR-C4)
indication: High-risk AML, relapse prophylaxis after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: HLA-A*02:01-positive, WT1-expressing high-risk AML; TCR inserted into EBV-specific donor CD8+ T cells and infused prophylactically post-HCT (not for active disease).
design: Phase 1/2 single-arm with concurrent comparative cohort
intervention_dose: Prophylactic post-HCT infusion of TCRC4-transduced EBV-specific donor CD8+ T cells

outcomes.name: RFS
outcomes.notes: 100% RFS at median 44 months after infusion (treated group)

outcomes.name: RFS
outcomes.notes: 54% RFS in similar-risk AML not given TTCR-C4; P=0.002 for the comparison

safety_summary: Prophylactic product engineered into EBV-specific CD8+ T cells to minimise GVHD; abstract reports long-term persistence and polyfunctionality without a per-term AE breakdown.
notes: Relapse-prevention (prophylaxis) evidence, not active-relapse salvage; gated on HLA-A*02:01 and superseded operationally by FH-WT1-E50. Comparator is a historical/concurrent cohort, so the survival contrast is confounded. Per-term safety not in the abstract; PMC/publisher full text not retrievable via available channels.

population_detail: HLA-A*24:02-restricted WT1-specific TCR (retroviral vector with siRNA silencing of endogenous TCR); two dose-escalation cohorts, transfers 4 weeks apart followed by WT1 peptide vaccine.
intervention_dose: Two WT1-siTCR T-cell transfers at a 4-week interval in a dose-escalating design, then sequential WT1 peptide vaccination

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: transient decrease in bone-marrow blasts with recovery of haematopoiesis

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.notes: 4 of 5 patients with persistent T cells at end of study survived >12 months

safety_summary: No adverse events attributable to normal-tissue recognition; TCR-T detected in blood for at least 8 weeks and persisted in 5 of 8 patients with retained WT1 reactivity.
notes: A*24:02 fallback lever, relevant only if the patient is A*02:01-negative. Small early-phase Japanese cohort; efficacy signals are transient blast reductions rather than remissions.

indication: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic-cell neoplasm (BPDCN), untreated or relapsed
population_detail: CD123-overexpressing BPDCN; 32 first-line and 15 previously treated; registration cohort for FDA approval. Not the patient's disease (AML) — mechanism/off-label precedent for the CD123 handle.
intervention_dose: Tagraxofusp 7 or 12 µg/kg IV on days 1-5 of each 21-day cycle
safety_summary: Capillary-leak syndrome in 19% (fatal in at least one patient in each dose subgroup); hepatic transaminase elevation and thrombocytopenia common. CLS is the characteristic and decision-relevant risk, especially in a fitness-unassessed patient.

toxicities.notes: associated with one death in each dose subgroup

notes: Registration study behind tagraxofusp's BPDCN approval; carries the CD123 mechanism as off-label precedent, not on-label AML support. Rates are all-grade from the abstract; per-grade table is in the full text.

population_detail: CD123+ R/R AML, ECOG 0-1, one or more prior AML treatments; recommended phase 2 dose expansion n=29.
intervention_dose: Pivekimab sunirine 0.045 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks (recommended phase 2 dose)
outcome: Overall response rate at recommended phase 2 dose
safety_summary: At the recommended phase 2 dose the most common grade 3+ treatment-related events were febrile neutropenia (10%), infusion reactions (7%) and anaemia (7%); one treatment-related death (1%) among 68 schedule-A patients. Dose-limiting toxicities were reversible veno-occlusive disease and neutropenia.

toxicities.notes: reversible; dose-limiting toxicity in escalation (0.180 and 0.450 mg/kg)

notes: Single-agent CD123 ADC activity in R/R AML that matches the patient's CD123 positivity; quantitative antigen-density selection is advisory and still pending. VOD signal is relevant given a planned second transplant.

indication: Primary induction failure / early-relapse refractory AML
population_detail: Adults with R/R AML; 42 in dose-finding and 46 at the 500 ng/kg/day RP2D. Efficacy reported for the 30 primary-induction-failure/early-relapse patients treated at RP2D.
intervention_dose: Flotetuzumab 500 ng/kg per day (RP2D) with week-1 step-up dosing, pre-treatment dexamethasone and tocilizumab as needed
outcome: CR/CRh in PIF/early-relapse patients at RP2D
safety_summary: Infusion-related reactions / cytokine release syndrome were the dominant toxicity and were largely grade 1-2; severe IRR/CRS was prevented with week-1 step-up dosing, pre-treatment dexamethasone, prompt tocilizumab and dose interruptions.

toxicities.notes: most frequent AE, largely grade 1-2; mitigated by step-up dosing, dexamethasone and tocilizumab

notes: CD123xCD3 bispecific with salvage activity in chemo-refractory AML, close to this patient's state; program has since been deprioritised by MacroGenics, so it is mechanism precedent rather than an open route. Per-grade CRS breakdown is in the full text, not the abstract.

indication: CD33-positive AML in untreated first relapse
population_detail: CD33+ AML in first relapse, no antecedent haematologic disorder, median age 61; three pooled open-label single-arm trials. Population is less heavily pretreated than this patient (no prior FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure or extramedullary disease).
intervention_dose: Gemtuzumab ozogamicin 9 mg/m2 IV over 2 hours, two doses at a 2-week interval

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: remission = <=5% marrow blasts, neutrophil recovery, transfusion independence (CR + CRp)

safety_summary: Grade 3/4 hyperbilirubinaemia (23%) and transaminase elevation (17%) with relatively low mucositis (4%) and severe nausea/vomiting (11%); no cardiotoxicity. Veno-occlusive disease is the characteristic class risk and matters given the planned second transplant.
notes: On-label, on-mechanism CD33 option, but single-agent depth in first relapse is modest (~30%) and this patient is further along with FLAG-IDA/venetoclax failure and extramedullary disease. Hepatic/VOD signal is relevant peri-transplant; quantitative CD33 density still pending.

indication: Active relapsed/refractory AML, age >=55, planned allogeneic HCT
population_detail: Patients >=55 with active R/R AML randomised to a 131I-apamistamab-led regimen before alloHCT vs conventional care (with crossover to apamistamab allowed on non-response). Enrolled patients heading to a first alloHCT.
intervention_dose: 131I-apamistamab (anti-CD45 radioconjugate) dosimetry-guided conditioning followed by allogeneic HCT

outcomes.name: HR_OS
outcomes.notes: OS not improved; heavy crossover (52% of control received apamistamab+alloHCT)

safety_summary: Grade >=3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 59.7% (apamistamab) vs 59.2% (conventional care); the targeted conditioning was well tolerated relative to its cytoreductive effect. OS was flat, plausibly because most control patients crossed over.
notes: Highest-grade evidence that CD45-targeted RIT can carry active high-burden R/R AML into an allo-HCT, directly relevant to conditioning a second transplant with an 85%-blast marrow. SIERRA enrolled patients heading to a first transplant, so prior-HCT eligibility is the axis to verify. Per-term AE breakdown not in the abstract.

indication: Advanced/metastatic solid tumors harbouring TP53 Y220C
population_detail: Heavily pretreated locally advanced/metastatic solid tumors with a TP53 Y220C mutation; PYNNACLE phase 1 dose escalation/optimization. Solid tumors only — no myeloid patients; responses restricted to KRAS wild-type tumors.
intervention_dose: Rezatapopt oral, continuous 21-day cycles; recommended phase 2 dose 2000 mg once daily with food (MTD 1500 mg twice daily)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.subgroup: KRAS wild-type, dose >=1150 mg once daily
outcomes.notes: all responders were TP53 Y220C + KRAS wild-type

safety_summary: Most common events were nausea (58%) and vomiting (44%); grade 3+ anaemia (16%) was the most frequent high-grade event and 2 patients (3%) discontinued for a treatment-related AE. GI toxicity was less frequent when given with food.
notes: Proof-of-concept for Y220C-selective p53 reactivation, but all data are in solid tumors and this patient's TP53 status is unconfirmed (2019 mutant vs 2026 negative on a limited assay) with Y220C not established. A low-positive/unconfirmed biomarker is a weaker predictor than a tier-matched confirmed one; the myeloid trial NCT06616636 has no results. Double contingency: confirm TP53 aberration, then confirm it is Y220C.

population_detail: Treatment-naive TP53-mutated AML, ECOG 0-2; eprenetapopt + venetoclax +/- azacitidine. Frontline population, not R/R — a line mismatch for this patient.
intervention_dose: Eprenetapopt 4.5 g/day IV days 1-4 + venetoclax 400 mg/day + azacitidine 75 mg/m2 days 1-7 (28-day cycles)
safety_summary: Grade 3+ events in >=20% were febrile neutropenia (47%), thrombocytopenia (37%), leukopenia (25%) and anaemia (22%); treatment-related serious events in 27% and one treatment-related death (sepsis).
notes: Pan-p53 reactivator, not Y220C-selective, and studied frontline rather than in R/R disease. The profile flags it as low-yield: the eprenetapopt+azacitidine phase 3 in TP53-mutant MDS missed its complete-remission primary endpoint and myeloid development has largely stopped. Kept so the board can weigh the pan-reactivator track against Y220C-selective rezatapopt.

intervention_label: Second allogeneic HCT for relapse after first allo-HCT
indication: Hematologic relapse of acute leukemia after first allogeneic HCT
population_detail: EBMT registry of 179 second transplants for relapse after a first transplant from matched related (n=75) or unrelated (n=104) donors; analysis of donor change. The patient's first HCT was from a matched sibling, so the related-donor subgroup is the relevant reference.
comparator: Original donor vs donor change for HSCT2
intervention_dose: Second allogeneic HCT (HSCT2), original or alternative donor

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.notes: 2-year OS; 16% after unrelated HSCT1 (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.47-0.98, P=.042)

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: CR after HSCT2 independent of donor; ~half subsequently relapsed

safety_summary: Registry outcome study; per-term toxicity and non-relapse mortality are not broken out in the abstract. Remission duration after HSCT1 and disease stage at HSCT2 were the dominant survival drivers.
notes: Anchors realistic HSCT2 expectations for this matched-sibling patient (~37% 2-year OS in the related-donor subgroup), and shows donor change is a valid but not clearly superior option. Long remission after HSCT1 (this patient ~6 years) favours survival; active high-burden disease at HSCT2 works against it.

intervention_label: FLAMSA-RIC sequential chemotherapy + reduced-intensity allo-HCT + prophylactic DLI
indication: High-risk AML and MDS (mostly progressive/refractory disease)
population_detail: 75 consecutive high-risk patients (59 progressive/refractory), 49% unfavourable karyotype; 31 with HLA-identical sibling donor. Fludarabine/cytarabine/amsacrine cytoreduction, then 4 Gy TBI/ATG/cyclophosphamide RIC, then prophylactic DLI from day +120.
intervention_dose: FLAMSA (fludarabine 30 mg/m2, cytarabine 2 g/m2, amsacrine 100 mg/m2 x4 days) -> 3 days rest -> RIC (4 Gy TBI + ATG + cyclophosphamide 80-120 mg/kg) -> allo-HCT -> prophylactic DLI from day +120
outcome: Complete remission after the sequential regimen

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.notes: 2-year OS; outcome of refractory/complex-cytogenetics patients equal to better-prognosis subgroups

safety_summary: GVHD and prophylactic-DLI-associated GVHD are the principal risks; survival was best with high CD34+ cell dose and limited GVHD. Per-term toxicity is not tabulated in the abstract.
notes: The FLAMSA-RIC sequencing this patient's plan is built on: it takes refractory AML with adverse cytogenetics straight to a reduced-intensity allo-HCT and reports outcomes for that hardest subgroup equal to lower-risk patients. 31 of 75 used HLA-identical sibling donors, matching the patient's donor situation.

intervention_label: Donor lymphocyte infusion (DLI) for AML relapse after allo-HCT
indication: AML in first haematological relapse after allogeneic HCT
population_detail: EBMT registry of 399 patients with AML in first relapse post-HCT; 171 treated with DLI vs 228 without. Multivariate analysis of survival drivers among DLI recipients.
intervention_dose: Donor lymphocyte infusion, alone or with cytoreduction, for first haematological relapse after HCT
outcome: 2-year overall survival, DLI vs no DLI

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.notes: 2-year OS; use of DLI independently favourable (P=.04) after adjustment

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.subgroup: DLI in remission or favourable karyotype

outcomes.name: OS_rate
outcomes.subgroup: DLI in aplasia or with active disease

safety_summary: GVHD is the characteristic DLI toxicity; the abstract reports survival rather than per-term AE rates. Clinical benefit was limited to a minority — best when DLI was given in remission or with favourable karyotype, worst in aplasia or active disease.
notes: Sets honest expectations for sibling DLI in this patient: relapse >5 months after HCT (here ~6 years) favours benefit, but 85% marrow blasts and adverse cytogenetics put him in the active-disease/high-burden group where 2-year OS is ~15%. Argues for cytoreduction before any DLI rather than DLI alone.

exclusion_reason: Biomarker mismatch and out of feature scope: revumenib acts through the menin-KMT2A interaction and its approval / AUGMENT-101 data are in KMT2A-rearranged (or NPM1-mutant) acute leukemia. This patient has KMT2A amplification (4 copies), a distinct lesion for which menin-inhibitor benefit is unproven, and no menin/KMT2A-rearrangement target is listed among the patient's targetable_features.
notes: Reviewed at the user's explicit request for an honest menin-inhibitor read. AUGMENT-101 is a real, positive trial in KMT2A-rearranged disease; the exclusion is on eligibility/biomarker grounds, not evidence quality.

exclusion_reason: Same biomarker mismatch as revumenib and out of feature scope: ziftomenib is approved in NPM1-mutant AML and studied in KMT2A-rearranged disease. This patient has neither a documented NPM1 mutation nor a KMT2A rearrangement (the lesion is KMT2A amplification), so no proven ziftomenib biomarker applies and none is among the targetable_features.
notes: Logged for completeness of the menin-inhibitor picture the profile asked about. No dedicated publication cited here to avoid an unverifiable identifier; COMET-001 enrolls NPM1-mutant/KMT2A-rearranged disease.

exclusion_reason: Population mismatch and program discontinuation: the CD123xCD3 bispecific was studied in MRD-positive AML/MDS and terminated. The MRD setting does not match this patient's overt high-burden relapse (~85% marrow blasts), and no pivotal efficacy publication anchors an evidence row.
notes: On-mechanism for the CD123 handle but no usable clinical-evidence publication; the CD123 bispecific evidence base is carried by the flotetuzumab row.

intervention_label: CBX-250 (TCR-mimetic bispecific T-cell engager targeting CG1/HLA-A*02:01)
indication: Relapsed/refractory AML, high-risk MDS, and CMML
population_detail: HLA-A*02:01-positive R/R myeloid leukemia; prior allogeneic HCT permitted once at least 60 days have elapsed.
design: First-in-human open-label phase 1 dose-escalation, single-agent (CROSSCHECK-001, NCT06994676)
intervention_dose: Subcutaneous; dose-escalation, recommended phase 2 dose not yet established
outcome: Trial in progress; no efficacy readout reported
safety_summary: Trial in progress, so there is no clinical safety or efficacy readout yet. As a CD3-engaging T-cell engager the anticipated class toxicity is cytokine release syndrome; the preclinical program reported high CG1/Cathepsin-G antigen selectivity with relative sparing of normal myeloid cells.
notes: On the patient's primary HLA-A*02:01 axis, but gated on the same pending HLA typing as the rest of that axis. Distinct advantage over the TCR-T options: an off-the-shelf T-cell engager with no autologous or donor cell manufacturing. Added after the initial screen, which missed the trial because CG1/Cathepsin-G was not a nominated feature. Identifiers left null: the ASH 2025 trial-in-progress abstract DOI could not be verified through available channels during this run (fail-closed per the reference-check protocol), so no identifier was guessed.
